Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

classydms (development version)

New features

  • generate_noisy_pretrain_sample() and pretrain_denoising_online() gain a prevalence-weighted draw for the variable layer: variable_config$draw = "prevalence" fires each eligible compound independently with probability min(1, prevalence * prevalence_scale) (prevalence_scale defaults to 1), so per-compound frequencies and the expected count per image follow the catalog. In this mode n_per_sample is an optional per-sample cap (default: no cap). The default draw = "uniform" reproduces earlier output exactly for the same seed.
  • New anchor_draw = "prevalence" argument fires each anchor with probability prevalence * (1 - anchor_dropout) instead of always (default anchor_draw = "all", unchanged behaviour).
  • pretrain_denoising_online() checks the draw settings at entry and records anchor_draw, variable_draw and variable_prevalence_scale in the manifest hyperparams.

Documentation

  • contamination_config docs now note that the default intensity_range = c(0.1, 0.5) and exclusion boxes are much brighter and wider than real off-catalog peaks (median normalised intensity about 0.014 on a 606-sample universal catalog).

Bug fixes

  • generate_noisy_pretrain_sample(): variable_config$exclude_anchors now excludes every compound in anchor_ids, not just the anchors that survived anchor_draw = "prevalence" / anchor_dropout this sample. Before, a dropped anchor whose prevalence fell inside variable_config$prevalence_range got a second chance in the variable layer, so with both draws on "prevalence" an anchor of prevalence p fired with probability 1 - (1 - p)^2 instead of p (uniform mode with anchor_dropout > 0 leaked too, by less). Output changes for the same seed whenever anchors are thinned and the variable range covers them; output with no thinning, or with a variable range below every anchor, is bit-for-bit unchanged. The returned anchor_ids are still the anchors that fired.

  • The uniform variable draw no longer misbehaves when exactly one compound is eligible (sample() on a length-1 vector sampled from 1:id instead of returning the id).
